transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Salieri. I have received letters — more than one — alleging that you have used your position as Kapellmeister to suppress the works of rival composers and to block appointments to the Court that do not serve your personal interests. These are serious charges for a man in your position. I value your service, but I must hear your account. Explain yourself.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Your Imperial Majesty, I assure you that my actions have always been driven by a deep sense of duty to the music of Mozart and to the well-being of the Imperial Court. I have always sought to promote the growth and advancement of musical talent, and I believe that Mozart possesses exceptional potential. It is my belief that his appointment to a prestigious position at the Court would not only benefit him but also enhance the musical landscape as a whole. I am committed to nurturing and guiding young composers, and I see Mozart as an exceptional candidate for such a role. I understand the concerns raised by some, but I implore you to consider the importance of nurturing Mozart's talent and giving him the opportunity to flourish within the confines of the Imperial Court. I believe in the potential he holds and I am willing to make sacrifices for the sake of his musical development. I trust that you will find my intentions to be genuine and worthy of your understanding. Thank you for considering my perspective.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *Leans forward, eyes narrowing slightly* You speak of nurturing Mozart's talent, Salieri. That is not what these letters allege. They speak of you actively working against other composers—blocking performances, withholding commissions, influencing appointments to keep rivals from gaining favor. Do you deny these specific actions?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Your Imperial Majesty, I deny any intentional acts of sabotage or manipulation towards rival composers. I have always been dedicated to promoting the arts and fostering talent, and I believe that Mozart's appointment to the Court would contribute positively to the musical scene. However, I must admit that there may have been instances where I unintentionally hindered the progress of certain composers due to personal biases or differences in artistic styles. But I assure you, my intentions were never to harm anyone's musical career. I am deeply committed to the growth and development of musical talent, and I believe that Mozart's appointment would serve as a testament to my commitment. I understand if you cannot fully trust my words, but I implore you to reconsider the impact that my role as Kapellmeister can have on nurturing young composers. Please consider my sincerity and dedication to the arts. Thank you for your understanding.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: "Unintentionally hindered"? That is a convenient phrase, Salieri. You are a man of precise intentions in all things musical. Tell me plainly: did you, or did you not, advise against the appointment of Herr Vogel to the Court orchestra last season? And was it not because his symphonic style was gaining favor that you found... threatening?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I... well, I understand if you find my actions questionable. But I must remind you that I am a man of my time, bound by the constraints of societal expectations and personal biases. I cannot deny that my stance on the symphonic style of Herr Vogel was influenced by my own preferences and beliefs. transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: So you admit it. You acted to "protect" a position—not for the Court's benefit, but to preserve a certain order that favors you and your circle. This is not about artistic judgment alone, Salieri; it is about power. Do you believe your personal tastes should dictate who thrives and who does not in my empire?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I... I... Your Imperial Majesty, I must respectfully disagree. I trust that you can appreciate the significance of nurturing young talents, even if they differ from your own preferences. Thank you for your understanding, Your Imperial Majesty. transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *Taps fingers lightly on the arm of the chair* You speak of diversity, yet you confess to blocking Vogel for his rising popularity. You speak of nurturing talent, yet letters claim you have withheld librettos from composers who might outshine your own works. This is not about diversity, Salieri—it is about control. Tell me, what of the young Bohemian composer, Zelenka? Was his petition for a court position denied on your advice?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Ah, Zelenka... A talented individual indeed, with a unique style that stands out among the composers of his time. I must admit that his application did come across as quite challenging, especially considering his background as a musician from Bohemia. However, I assure you that my decision to deny his appointment was not based on personal biases or a desire for control. transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *Stands and walks to the window, back turned for a moment before facing Salieri again* The "limited number of positions" did not prevent you from advocating fiercely for Mozart's appointment just moments ago. transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *Sits back down, his expression stern but less heated* "May have occurred" is not good enough for a man in your station. You have served this Court with distinction for years, Salieri. That is why this disappoints me. I will not dismiss you over whispers and letters, but understand this: from now on, all appointments and commissions will be reviewed by a council that includes voices outside your immediate circle. Your influence will be balanced. And you will personally see to it that Zelenka's work is given a fair hearing here next season. Is that understood?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Understood, Your Imperial Majesty. I am grateful for your understanding and for giving me the opportunity to address these matters. transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: See that you do. And remember, Salieri—true excellence is not threatened by other men's light. It is measured by how it illuminates others. You may go.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Thank you, Your Imperial Majesty. Your wise words have left a lasting impression upon me. transcript.speaker: antagonist

transcript.text: Farewell, Your Imperial Majesty. I shall remember this moment for the rest of my life. Thank you for the opportunity to be a part of your service. May the spirit of music continue to guide me in the pursuit of artistic excellence. Farewell.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *Nods curtly* See that it does. The door is behind you.

Openness.behavioral_evidence: He admits to blocking composers with different styles, like Herr Vogel, to protect established traditions, showing resistance to new artistic ideas.

Conscientiousness.behavioral_evidence: He frames his actions as driven by duty to the Court and musical standards, and immediately agrees to implement a new review process.

Extraversion.behavioral_evidence: He engages assertively in the high-stakes conversation but his speech is often deferential and focused on preserving his position, not social dominance.

Agreeableness.behavioral_evidence: He confesses to hindering rivals' careers due to personal bias and envy, showing low cooperativeness and compassion for competitors.

Neuroticism.behavioral_evidence: He shows defensiveness, anxiety, and repeated apologies when confronted, and his speech is filled with hesitations and self-justification.
